rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should test a balanced multimodal configuration with advanced components. This experiment tests multimodal (RNA + image) with scvi_n200 (RNA encoder), ViT (image encoder), transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion - all components that are likely to yield strong performance. This configuration explores key design choices (encoder types, aggregation, fusion) that are critical for multimodal success, maximizing information gain with the first experiment.

The existing evidence shows config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieves 0.725 validation accuracy. This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with resnet50 while keeping RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion method identical. It clarifies whether the choice of image encoder significantly impacts performance, a critical design decision with high uncertainty. This balances exploitation (building on successful multimodal/multiprofile setup) and exploration (testing alternative image encoders).

The existing evidence shows config_039 (ViT + transformer + weighted fusion) has the highest accuracy (0.725). However, uncertainty remains about whether using ResNet50 with avgpool aggregation (config_027) could yield better performance. This experiment tests a critical design choice (image encoder + aggregation) that could improve accuracy while building on the successful multimodal/multiprofile setup.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and transformer aggregation (e.g., config_039) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests using pca_n2000 RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion, exploring if a different RNA encoder could maintain high performance while keeping the effective aggregation method. It clarifies the impact of RNA encoder choices on accuracy, balancing exploration of key components with prior success in aggregation methods.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_039) yields the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests changing the fusion method to concat, which could clarify if the fusion strategy significantly impacts performance. This is the best use of the next experiment as it explores a critical design choice in the top-performing setup.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (config_039: 0.724989 accuracy) outperform those with resnet50 (config_013: 0.713087). This experiment tests resnet50 image encoder with concat fusion, comparing it to the top-performing vit_l-based models. It clarifies whether image encoder choice or fusion method has greater impact, balancing exploration of resnet50 and exploitation of the current top configuration.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l image encoder and weighted fusion (e.g., config_039) achieve the highest accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with resnet50 image encoder, a new combination that could improve performance. It clarifies whether switching RNA encoders or image encoders impacts accuracy, balancing exploration of new components against exploitation of proven settings.

The existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation with weighted fusion (config_039) and transformer with concat fusion (config_021) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests avgpool aggregation with concat fusion, which could clarify if aggregation method impacts performance. It balances exploration of aggregation techniques while maintaining high-performing RNA/image encoders, leveraging prior success with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_039) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests avgpool aggregation with the same RNA/image encoders and weighted fusion to determine if aggregation method impacts performance. It clarifies whether transformer aggregation is optimal or if avgpool could yield better results, leveraging the strong evidence from top-performing configurations.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_039) achieve the highest accuracy (0.724989). However, config_050 uses scvi_n200 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion, which has not been tested. This experiment tests whether using resnet50 instead of imagenet_vit_l with avgpool and concat could yield better performance, addressing uncertainty about image encoder choice and aggregation methods. It is the best use of the final experiment to explore a promising yet untested combination.
